decisions.reason: This modular trommel screen is a clear extension of an already accepted machine line and, given the firm's deep screening know-how and positive early reception, management would expect to improve rather than withdraw it.

Mobile high-speed flail shredders fit closely with the firm's established mobile waste-processing machinery capabilities, and a dedicated product page suggests enough commitment and learning potential to continue.

A mobile high-speed grinder is still close to the firm's core processing expertise, but the weaker website presence indicates more uncertainty, so management would keep it while monitoring market uptake and technical feedback.
A stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's existing stationary and shredding competences and its resource-saving strategic direction, making continued development more likely than exit.

This green-waste grinder targets a familiar customer segment in biomass and composting and builds on related grinder knowledge, so the firm would likely retain it despite limited early market evidence.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly related to the firm's established shredding and plant business, and the dedicated product presentation signals sufficient confidence to keep them on the market.
